rejected_alternative: Mal.4.1 or 4:2 alone was rejected because judgment and healing contrast completes at 4:3.

Mal.4.1-3 without parent hydration was rejected because 'For' makes it the prior movement's outcome.
convergence_defense.defensible_basis: Correlated paragraph marks plus a complete antithetical oracle justify a child; causal opening and repeated group vocabulary make hydration nonoptional.

source_observations.text: “For behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace, when all the proud and all who work wickedness will be stubble. The day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
You shall tread down the wicked; for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I make,” says Yahweh of Armies.

working_title: Moses remembrance and Elijah sending coda
deciding_marker_or_seam: After pe, 4:4 commands 'Remember the law of Moses ... at Horeb'; 4:5 begins 'Behold, I will send you Elijah,' and 4:6 gives kinship-turning purpose plus the lest-I-strike-with-herem close.
boundary_rationale: After the pe, the remembrance command in 4:4 and the sending formula in 4:5 form coordinated closing panels whose reconciliation purpose and curse-risk close arrive in 4:6. Neither Moses, Elijah, the heart-turning purpose, nor the final threat may surface apart from the paired coda.
rejected_alternative: The 4:4 | 4:5-6 split was rejected because they form a paired Torah-and-prophet coda.
Mal.4.5-6 alone was rejected because later reuse can erase the Moses frame.
Mal.4.6 alone was rejected because herem is the coda's consequence, not a standalone curse.
counterevidence: WEB paragraphs before 4:4 and 4:5 and the imperative-to-future shift support two dependent internal panels.
Mal.4.5 has a new “Behold” onset and later reuse pressure, but purpose and curse-risk require the whole coda.
defensible_basis: Imperative remembrance, coordinated sending, purpose, and final risk function as a paired book coda after a source-supported seam.
